title: Whistlejacket by George Stubbs
episode: Is 'Whistlejacket' the most famous horse in art? | National Gallery
description: Stubbs’s life-size portrait of a racehorse rearing against a blank background, painted around 1762 for the Marquess of Rockingham. Stubbs had spent 18 months dissecting horses to learn their anatomy.

title: Venus and Mars by Sandro Botticelli
episode: Botticelli’s 'Venus and Mars': A depiction of Renaissance love | National Gallery
description: Botticelli’s long panel of the goddess of love awake and the god of war asleep, while little satyrs play with his armor. It was probably made around 1485 for a Florentine bedroom.

title: Belshazzar’s Feast by Rembrandt
episode: Rembrandt's Belshazzar's Feast | How does Rembrandt capture a king’s downfall?
description: Rembrandt’s dramatic scene from the Book of Daniel, about 1636: a hand writes on the wall at a Babylonian king’s banquet, and he turns in terror. The Hebrew letters are arranged in columns, as a rabbi friend may have advised.

title: The Ugly Duchess by Quinten Massys
episode: How does this painting link Leonardo da Vinci to Alice's Adventures in Wonderland? The Ugly Duchess
description: A satirical portrait of an old woman in an outdated low-cut dress, painted in Antwerp around 1513. It probably inspired John Tenniel’s Duchess in Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland.

title: Saint Jerome in His Study by Antonello da Messina
episode: A guide to 'Saint Jerome in his Study' by Antonello da Messina | Working from home
description: A tiny painting of the scholar saint reading in a study set inside a vast Gothic hall, with a lion, a peacock, and a cat. Antonello, from Sicily, was one of the first Italians to master oil paint.

title: The Entombment by Michelangelo
episode: Why did Michelangelo leave 'The Entombment' unfinished? | National Gallery
description: An unfinished early painting of Christ’s body carried to the tomb, attributed to Michelangelo around 1500, with blank areas where he never got to the paint. A rare chance to see how he worked.

title: The Execution of Maximilian by Édouard Manet
episode: Why did Degas have to reassemble Manet's 'Execution of Maximilian'? | National Gallery
description: Manet’s painting of the shooting of Maximilian, the Austrian-born emperor of Mexico, in 1867. It was cut into pieces after his death, and Degas bought the fragments and had them reassembled.
